title: Malaysia Tourist SIM Card: Collect at KLIA2 or Use eSIM
metaDescription: Book a tourist SIM card for Malaysia online and collect it at KLIA2 or Lalaport BBCC, buy one at a telco counter with your passport, or use an eSIM.

contentBlocks.content: There are three ways to get mobile data as a tourist in Malaysia. Book a Teeko travel SIM online and collect it at the tour centre at KLIA2 or at Lalaport BBCC. Buy a prepaid SIM at a telco counter in KLIA2, with your original passport in hand. Or install an eSIM on your phone before you fly. Pre-booking suits you if you want your plan settled before you land. A counter suits you if you want staff to set the SIM up for you. An eSIM suits you if your phone supports it and you want data as soon as you switch off flight mode.
Key Takeaways

What do I need to buy a SIM card in Malaysia as a tourist? At a telco counter, your original passport, plus your visa if you needed one to enter. Since 27 February 2026, photocopies and photos of a passport are not accepted.
Can I collect a SIM at KLIA2? Yes. Book a Teeko travel SIM online, then show the QR code from your booking email at the tour centre at KLIA2 or at Lalaport BBCC in Bukit Bintang.
Where are the SIM counters at KLIA2? CelcomDigi is on the Arrival Level public concourse. U Mobile is on Level 2 Arrivals in Gateway@klia2, the mall joined to the terminal.
How long does a tourist line last? A tourist prepaid line from a Malaysian telco runs for up to 90 days. Then the service ends.
Do I need a plastic SIM if my phone takes an eSIM? No. You can install an eSIM before you fly. A Malaysian telco eSIM is still a prepaid line, so expect the same passport check.

Rules and counter locations checked on 11 October 2026. Sources are named in each section below.
Option 1: book a Teeko travel SIM and collect it on arrival

Pick a package on the travel SIM page, sign in with your email, and choose the date you will collect it. You receive an email with a verification code and a QR code. Show it at the tour centre at KLIA2 or at the tour centre at Lalaport BBCC in Bukit Bintang, and you leave with your SIM.
There are five packages, all from the provider MyTeekoSIM:

Prices and durations as listed on 11 October 2026. Each package lists 4G/5G connectivity across Malaysia, including major cities and popular tourist destinations. You insert the SIM and start using it. It works in Malaysia only.
You must be 18 or over to book, or 16 to 18 with a parent or guardian. If your plans change, cancel the booking from "My Travel SIM Bookings" on your profile page.

Landing at KLIA2? Collect it there and you have data before you look for your bus. Coming in on a bus from Singapore that ends at Lalaport BBCC? Collect your SIM there; the Lalaport BBCC hub guide shows you around. Compare the travel SIM packages and pick your collection date.
Option 2: buy a SIM at a telco counter in KLIA2

Malaysian telcos sell prepaid SIMs at KLIA2, and staff register and set up the SIM for you. Since 27 February 2026 the registration rules for tourists are stricter, so check what to bring before you queue.
What to bring

Bring your original passport, and your visa if you needed one to enter Malaysia. Photocopies, photos and scans are not accepted. Your name, passport number, issuing country and expiry date are recorded. These are the rules from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) that took effect on 27 February 2026 (MCI Group report, 27 February 2026).

At the counter, staff read your passport in a passport reader with a facial recognition check (U Mobile prepaid registration guidelines, checked 11 October 2026). Some telcos also ask for a hotel booking or other proof of where you are staying (CMLink Malaysia, checked 11 October 2026). Keep your hotel confirmation on your phone or on paper.
Each telco can register up to two prepaid SIMs to a non-Malaysian (MalaysianWireless on the MCMC standards, 28 January 2026).
Where the counters are

• CelcomDigi Store KLIA2. S2-2-1C03A, Arrival Level public concourse, Terminal KLIA2 (CelcomDigi store locator).
  • U Mobile. Level 2 Arrivals, Gateway@klia2 (U Mobile store finder).

Both checked on 11 October 2026. Other telcos and phone kiosks trade in the arrival area and in Gateway@klia2. Plans and prices change, so compare them at the counter. The KLIA2 arrival hall guide shows the walk from customs.
How long a tourist line lasts

A tourist prepaid line runs for up to 90 days, then the telco ends the service (CMLink Malaysia; MCI Group). That covers a normal holiday. Staying longer on a work or student pass is a different registration; ask the telco.
One more thing for the arrival queue: fill in your Malaysia Digital Arrival Card before you fly. The MDAC guide takes you through it.
Option 3: use an eSIM

An eSIM is a SIM profile you download to your phone instead of a plastic card. If your phone supports it, install it at home and switch it on when you land. You skip the counter queue. The beginner's guide to eSIM shows how to check your phone.

An eSIM from a Malaysian telco is still a prepaid line, so expect the same passport registration as at the counter. Travel eSIMs from international sellers have their own terms. Before you pay, read which Malaysian network the plan uses and how many days it covers. If your phone does not take an eSIM, book a Teeko travel SIM or go to a counter instead.
Once you are online: from KLIA2 into the city

Your data matters most in the first hour. You need it for your bus e-ticket, for Grab, and for the map to your hotel. Airport buses leave from the Transportation Hub on Level 1 of KLIA2; the KLIA2 bus station guide shows the way down. The bus to KL Sentral takes about an hour. The KLIA2 to KL Sentral guide compares it with the train and a taxi.

contentBlocks.content: Staying in Bukit Bintang? Take the bus from KLIA2 to Lalaport BBCC instead. It ends at an indoor hub near Bukit Bintang, and the tour centre there is a Teeko travel SIM collection point. The KLIA2 to Bukit Bintang guide covers the last stretch. When you fly home, the guide to a taxi to KLIA helps you plan the ride back.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I buy a SIM card at KLIA2?

Yes, you can buy a SIM card at KLIA2. CelcomDigi has a store on the Arrival Level public concourse, and U Mobile has one on Level 2 Arrivals in Gateway@klia2. Bring your original passport. Or book a Teeko travel SIM online and collect it at the tour centre at KLIA2.
Can I register a Malaysian SIM with a photo of my passport?

You cannot register a Malaysian prepaid SIM with a photo or photocopy of your passport. Since 27 February 2026, telcos need your original passport, and your visa if you needed one to enter. Take your passport to the counter.
How long is a tourist SIM valid in Malaysia?
A tourist prepaid SIM from a Malaysian telco is valid for up to 90 days. After that, the telco ends the service. Plan a new registration if you stay longer on a different pass.
Where do I collect a Teeko travel SIM?

You collect a Teeko travel SIM at the tour centre at KLIA2 or at the tour centre at Lalaport BBCC in Bukit Bintang. Show the verification code and QR code from your booking email. Book your travel SIM and choose your collection date.
How much is a Teeko travel SIM?
A Teeko travel SIM costs RM25 for 3 days, RM28 for 4 days, RM30 for 5 days, RM35 for 6 days and RM39 for 7 days. Pick the package that covers your trip on the travel SIM page.
Can I cancel a Teeko travel SIM booking?
Yes, you can cancel a Teeko travel SIM booking. Open "My Travel SIM Bookings" on your profile page and cancel it there.
Conclusion

For a tourist SIM card in Malaysia, book a Teeko travel SIM if you want your plan settled before you land, and collect it at KLIA2 or Lalaport BBCC. Go to a telco counter if you want staff to set it up, and bring your original passport. Use an eSIM if your phone supports it. Then get into the city: book your KLIA2 to KL Sentral bus on ttklia.com before you fly.
